newsitem.title: USA: GSEs tack through prepayments with callable debt.
newsitem.headline: GSEs tack through prepayments with callable debt.

text.p: U.S. Government Sponsored Enterprises (GSEs), or government sponsored business activities, have come to rely on callable debt to manage interest rate risk.

The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp (Freddie Mac), the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae) are congressionally chartered corporations.

Freddie Mac and Fannie Mae purchase residential mortgages in the secondary market from savings and loans, banks and mortgage bankers. The mortgages are then securitized for sale into the capital markets.
Sallie Mae performs a similar role in the student loan market. It purchases student loans from lenders and provides financing to state student loan agencies.
For Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the callable agency debt allows the GSEs to manage their mortgage portfolios, but prepayments on Sallie Mae's 10-year student loans have not been as great a concern.
"Prepayments on the underlying asset is not a factor in our decision. We call debt when it makes economic sense to do so, principally when rates have gone down," said a spokesman for Sallie Mae.
But for Fannie Mae, callable agency debt has allowed it to build its mortgage portfolio.

"It has been an instrumental part in allowing us to grow our mortgage portfolio. We look at the inherent prepayment sensitivity to each mortgage product and tailor debt to each mortgage product," said Joseph Amato, vice president of portfolio strategy at Fannie Mae.
At Freddie Mac "we finance our risk with callable debt and a mix of short- and long-term debt," said Douglas Robinson, a spokesman.
Robinson added that Freddie Mac designs "a mix of long- and shorter-term debt to match the cashflow characteristics of mortgages in the retained portfolio."
Fannie Mae's Amato praised the callable debt instrument for its flexibility.
"If Treasury rates rise, then mortgage rates rise and then agency debt extends as well," he said.
Robinson said Freddie Mac "further refined the mix of debt with different off-balance sheet instruments such as interest rate contracts, floors and caps, as well as interest rate floors."
While mortgage bankers are busy hedging their portfolios -- low rates erode servicing portfolio values, but help bolster originations -- the GSEs's role is different.
"Mortgage bankers are not portfolio investors. We are a buyer and holder of mortgages, while mortgage bankers earn a revenue stream through originations and servicing," said Amato.
By and large, Robinson said, Freddie Mac is not "into speculating on interest rates when managing the portfolio."

In the first six months of 1997, Fannie Mae had $216.262 billion in outstanding long-term debt. Of that, $131.329 billion is fixed-rate callable debt. The GSE issued, in the first six months of 1997, $19.55 billion of fixed-rate callable debt and $13.07 billion fixed-rate bullet debt.
In the period ended June 30, Freddie Mac issued $10.76 billion of callable debt and the GSE had called about $3.87 billion of debt, while $1.23 billion has matured.
